result:
I've completed cycle 2. Here's what I did and what I could not do.

## C2-A — the three failing sweeps (fixed)

All three were one defect **in the test, not the emitted document**. jq evaluates the *argument* of `index()` against the *input* of `index()`, so `$s | index(.value.state)` asks the published array for a `.value` field. The document shape already matched `docs/LIFECYCLE-CONTRACT.md`. Fixed by binding the value first (`.value.state as $st | select(($s | index($st)) == null)`).

The same shape made a **fourth sweep silently vacuous**: `every reason code in a live result is published` evaluated `$pub | index(.)` — the array searching for itself, always found at index 0, never selecting anything. It was green while guarding nothing. Fixed the same way.

Each of the four sweeps is now followed by an **executable falsifiability control** that injects one out-of-set value and requires the sweep to report exactly it.

## The fourth failure the evidence counted but didn't show

`run-tests.sh` prints a 40-line tail, so `215 passed, 4 failed` showed only three. The fourth was `and an uncheckable live dependency exits 5`, and it was a real product defect: `afk_validator_verdict` mapped *every* non-zero validator exit to "rejected", so a validator that couldn't answer (exit 2) produced a deterministic not-ready and exit 3 where the contract requires transient-unavailable and exit 5. Fixed: only exit 1 is a policy verdict; anything else is the new `VALIDATOR_VERDICT_UNAVAILABLE`, transient, exit 5. An unanswered negative fixture no longer counts as a rejection either.

## C2-B — completion monitor + cleanup (implemented)

New `lib/afk-monitor.sh` + `monitor` command (`--register`, `--reconcile`, `--cleanup --live`): durable on-disk watch, completion only from a supervised delivery, retention→reconciliation→acknowledgement keyed by `delivery_id`, heartbeat/terminal faults that never become results, provenance-bound cleanup that fails closed. One bounded pass per invocation — no `--wait`, no rolling poll. New gate `tests/lifecycle-dispatch-tests.sh` covers every named regression from both lists against real Git repos and a stubbed Orca.

Two interpretations I flagged in the record: "must not duplicate review dispatch" is proven via the effects a replay must not repeat (nothing here launches a reviewer); and the delivery transport is modelled as a durable inbox directory.

## C2-C — frozen-requirement collision (not implemented, per the ruling)

`tests/lifecycle-tests.sh:1431` enumerates `agent-stamp-validate` in the stub set, `:1448` asserts `no external binary was invoked` for default `status`, and `:1454` asserts `validator fixtures NOT_EVALUATED`. Running fixtures by default fails all three, and the same guarantee is stated in the contract document. Fixtures stayed behind `--live`; the exact assertions are recorded under a "Frozen-requirement collision" heading with the one-line change it would take. Disposition is yours.

## Gates

**Not executed.** This session has Read/Glob/Grep/Write only — no shell — so `bash tests/lifecycle-tests.sh`, `bash tests/run-tests.sh` and `git diff --check` could not be run. Nothing above claims they pass. Highest-risk areas for your re-run, in order: shellcheck on the new ~700-line `lib/afk-monitor.sh`; the new dispatch gate's real `git worktree`/`branch -d`/`push --delete` usage; and the schema↔document `reason_codes` comparison, which now carries 40 new codes and fails loudly on a single mismatch.

Diff size is now roughly **4,700 reviewable lines, ~6× the single-PR budget**. Per the standing constraint I did not restructure to shrink it; the recommended stacked split now has a fourth layer (the dispatch monitor).
